name: First language models
strandNote: Optional for every quant role. For machine learning research roles, and for using and building AI tools with judgement.
description: Build character models of names, from a table of counts to a network with embeddings, and judge them on names they never saw.

requires.why: Trains the one-layer network with the array autograd and its softmax cross-entropy.
Reads the loss as a cross-entropy, in nats and in bits.
Normalised counts are the maximum likelihood estimate, derived as for a coin.
Next-word tables by counting, and sampling from them, first met in Stage 0.
Judges a model once on held-out names, as a backtest judges a rule once out of sample.

lessonNames.l2-the-counts-are-best: The counts are the best table
lessonNames.l4-bigram-as-network: The same model as a network

lessonObjectives.l1-counting-pairs: Build the 27 by 27 table of letter pairs from a list of names.
lessonObjectives.l2-the-counts-are-best: Derive that normalised counts maximise the likelihood of a bigram model, and smooth the zero counts.
lessonObjectives.l3-one-loss-two-units: Compute the average negative log-likelihood in nats and in bits, and read it as a cross-entropy.
lessonObjectives.l4-bigram-as-network: Train a one-layer network on one-hot letters with softmax and reach the counting model's loss.
lessonObjectives.l5-three-letters-of-context: Build a dataset of three-letter contexts and next letters from a list of names.
lessonObjectives.l6-letters-as-points: Look up embeddings as rows of a matrix, and see why that equals a one-hot product.
lessonObjectives.l7-the-mlp-model: Build the forward pass of an embedding, a tanh hidden layer and a softmax output, and count its parameters.
lessonObjectives.l8-minibatches-and-rates: Train on minibatches and pick a learning rate from a sweep.
lessonObjectives.l9-sampling-names: Write a sampler that draws names letter by letter from a model with a seeded generator.
lessonObjectives.l10-train-dev-test: Split names into train, dev and test sets, and say what each one is for.
lessonObjectives.l11-overfitting: Watch the training loss fall while the dev loss rises, and choose a model by its dev loss.
lessonObjectives.l12-temperature: Divide the logits by a temperature and see the trade between safe and varied samples.
